overview: Medieval Norway's surviving stave churches reveal sophisticated woodworking and the adaptation of Christian architecture to Scandinavian building traditions.

items.text: Urnes translates the basilica plan into a timber building, using columns, arches and carefully framed roofs.
Its sill frame rests on stone foundations, contrasting with remains of an earlier structure whose posts entered the ground.
Eleventh-century carved elements were reused in the later church, preserving interlaced animal ornament.
Twelfth-century figurative capitals and medieval liturgical objects show the continuing development of Christian visual culture.
